title: Lazy Pig’s Gift
text: “Elmelo, Kou, sing.”
“It’s getting pretty late, so why don’t we do that in the morning? Or we could move somewhere lively and do it there.”
“Okaaay!”
Father watched this exchange between Kou and Elephant with a warm, approving look on his face.

“Once you’re done making the clothing materials, Yuki-chan should go chat with the Filolial-samas, and Kou, why don’t you go with Elephant to Zeltoble and visit Big Sister’s group? You can sing happily together with Elephant there.”
I’ll show you the way, I say.
“Yes, ma’am!”
“Got it!”
“How convenient that we can travel there so easily. As for the singing… please, a proper private room in Zeltoble.”
Elephant was quite the celebrity over there, after all. It seemed embarrassing for her to have her singing talent become known.
“That’s certainly heartwarming, Motoyasu-kun, Elmelo-san. Thanks, everyone. Well then, I’m off.”

Father threw on his robe and headed out, indeed. He was also handling slave purchases while he was at it—apparently something he’d been asked to look into. We had Big Sister confirm the details afterward. This was Father’s first day of activity running his slave-trading circus caravan, I say. The rest of us proceeded according to plan as well.

About two days had passed since the circus opened to the public. From the following day onward, Big Sister began accompanying him during purchases to verify things. Rather than stopping by the circus tent, she’d send them straight back to the treatment clinic in Zeltoble. It seemed she’d managed to find and purchase one slave from a village and bring them along to join us. And then, word came that a customer had shown up during the day wanting to conduct a slave transaction on the spot, so Father ended up handling the negotiation as our representative.
“Yes, yes, welcome, welcome to the circus. We do purchases here, but we’re not selling yet, I’m afraid.”
Father, doing his best impression of a monster merchant, proceeded to negotiate with the visitor.
“Bow!”
Wolf stood waiting behind Father as usual.
“Bwee!”
“Bow?”
The slave the customer had brought along let out something that sounded distinctly like admiration directed at Wolf, and Wolf tilted her head slightly in confusion.
“Huh? You want to work here? And this ‘gift’ is…”
Father found himself negotiating as though this were the most natural customer interaction in the world, indeed.
“Bwee, bwe-bwe-bwe, bwee.”
“What seems to be the matter?”

The Siltvelt envoy approached Father to ask. At the same moment, Father glanced my way as well, so I hurried over to join them. And there—I spotted the culprit. Though the slave that had let out the admiring cry toward Wolf was a pig, so I couldn’t be entirely certain… but wasn’t that Keel? Somehow, that was the feeling I got, I say.
“One moment, please.”
Father called the visitor to a halt like that, then stepped a little ways off to speak with me and the Siltvelt envoy.
“So apparently there’s someone here who wants to work for us—not as a slave, mind you—and they’ve brought along a slave as a ‘gift.’”
“That is extremely suspicious. Why, of all places, would they want to work here specifically? Could they not be someone in Melromarc’s pocket?”

“No, actually, here’s the thing. This person flat-out admitted they’d figured out that Motoyasu-kun and I are Heroes, and then on top of that, declared—quite boldly, mind you—that they want to help out because otherwise their parents would scold them for not having proper standing as a collaborator.”
“I see.”
“Motoyasu-kun, is this someone you know from a loop or something?”
“Indeed I do… That one is Lazy Pig, an incredibly lazy creature, but when it comes to business and survival instincts, it has a terrifyingly sharp nose, I say.”

I’d completely forgotten, since there’d been no sign of it in recent loops. Now that I thought about it, back during the loop where I reunited with Fleon-chan, after I’d had the Crimson Swine drink Ouroboros Deadly Poison, it had fled from me with everything it had, and I hadn’t seen it since. Given the timing, it wasn’t at all strange for it to have sniffed things out by now. And to add insult to injury, bringing along a proper gift as well—how thoroughly troublesome, I say.
“That one seems remarkably forthcoming about revealing their true motives.”
“Their parents belong to the Queen’s faction, apparently.”
“Ah, one of the people not aligned with that King and Princess, then.”
“Keep talking with them much longer and they’ll start saying you might as well just enslave them and let them join in, indeed.”
Indeed—back when we ran the merchant caravan through Melromarc, that one had even gone so far as to get enslaved just to slip into Father’s ranks.
“Doesn’t seem to pose any harm, but what do you think?”
“I think it finds me to be an eyesore, I say.”
“Hmm…”
Father crossed his arms and groaned.
“Bwe-bwe-bwe, bwe.”
Lazy Pig oinked at Father from a distance.
“No, even if you tell me straight to my face that you’ll leak information about the Melromarc side through your connections…”
“It does sound like it could be useful, though.”
“And where in the world did it dig up that slave it brought as a gift… If that’s Keel, this is going to be a headache. Could we just buy the slave separately?”

Why on earth had Lazy Pig managed to find Keel in the first place? Sure, if you threw enough money at the problem you could probably track someone down, but to bring her along so effortlessly? Come to think of it, the gift from the last time the loop reset had been similar too—was Lazy Pig secretly some kind of monster of observation, or what?
“Hm? You know this one too?”

Motoyasu, you’ve gone and put your foot in your mouth again, haven’t you? I could’ve sworn I heard my own voice saying that inside my head. But playing dumb here would only cause trouble later when it came time to retrieve Keel. More than anything, if Lazy Pig ended up taking Keel under its wing, it’d be a headache come purchase time regardless of what I said now. Given Lazy Pig’s business instincts, it seemed unlikely to let go of Keel even if I refused outright here. The end result would probably be the same either way, I supposed.
“It’s a dog-type demi-human, isn’t it?”
“It looks to me like a child of the Nui species. It seems quite excited looking at Wolf.”
Wolf, for her part, tilted her head at being addressed so.
“Handsome,” or something along those lines, was probably what was being said about her.
“Keel is a slave who can switch between pig and dog forms, indeed, and hails from the same hometown as Big Sister.”
“Given that it also possesses the ability to transform into a beastman, that would make it a Wa-Nui species, then.”
“From pig to dog… Motoyasu-kun, given that most women appear as pigs to you, does that mean… wait, that child is a girl?”
Father stared intently at Keel.
“At that age it’s difficult to determine gender by scent alone, so we can’t say for certain either, but at a glance, that one looks like nothing but a boy to me.”
“Guess Motoyasu-kun’s sensors are more accurate, then? Wolf!”
“Bow!”
Called by Father, Wolf trotted over happily.
“Wolf, can you tell if that child over there is a girl?”
“Wow? Wo-wow!?”
At being asked, Wolf sniffed around curiously and finally seemed to arrive at a look of realization.
“Seems like the answer’s a yes, then.”

Keel was Luna-chan’s pet slave, indeed. Come to think of it, during the previous loop, Luna-chan had gone somewhat berserk precisely because Keel hadn’t been around. She’d become fixated on clinging to Ren nonstop, and had demanded that I turn Ren into an inult. The sheer intensity of her fury had been a truly terrifying thing to behold. So, if at all possible, I did want to secure Keel here. But Lazy Pig, I did not want.
“If she’s a friend of Raphtalia-chan’s, I’d like to purchase her if we can, but…”
“Melromarc folk have no place in this circus—expel it at once, I say.”
And with that, I subtly sent a mental message to the Siltvelt envoy: rather than letting Father handle the mediation, you should be the one to snatch just Keel and send Lazy Pig packing.
“If it’s even willing to accept a slave crest and place itself under our authority, then perhaps it would be fine to accept.”
This incompetent fool! You’re supposed to be receiving my pressure loud and clear, I say!
“In that case, allow me to lay out some rather strict terms and see if we can hammer out an agreement.”
“You must not proceed in the direction of accepting the offer, I say!”

I protested as much, but Lazy Pig went ahead and hashed out terms with Father, the Siltvelt envoy, and the monster merchant’s subordinates respectively, and just like that, its position within the circus was decided, with Keel thrown in as the accompanying gift. From what I understood, its primary role would be managing the slaves kept for sale—not the ones under protection—along with negotiating purchases of necessary sundries. Father would still manage the ledger himself, but Lazy Pig would assist with that as well. Apparently, when the circus performed its first act and Father was too tired, Lazy Pig would even step in as a stand-in. It donned a mask and took on the role of whipping a mixed-breed lizardman and a rabbit-man. Lazy Pig actually had a decent figure underneath it all, so wearing risqué outfits and playing the seductress proved quite popular with the men—separately from Father’s own popularity, mind you. Thanks to its family connections, it also handled publicity, quietly spreading word of the slave-trading tent’s name. It even helped broker deals to secure land, apparently proving genuinely useful—which was, frankly, infuriating! And then… whenever it had a spare moment, it started taking naps on the safety net set up beneath where the trapeze act was planned. Grrrrgh! I say! The sight of it napping on the net above during practice was an absolute eyesore, indeed.
